used.how: the busiest chip's FPU pace (6.77 us a 32-row tile) set the relays' per-tile budget (~115 cycles a helper) that explained the first version's +20 ms and judged each fix
pack_bfp8_rows built as 32 per-chip programs (its own row0) in one prepared MeshProgramDescriptor: a prepared launch costs ~90-100 us either way
pack_bfp8_rows takes only common runtime args (row0, items, addresses), no per-core args
the host has slack after layer ~5, so the one extra prepared launch a MoE layer was accepted instead of folding the pack into the dispatch
kept the 6208 B fabric payload (MOE_BLOCK_SPLIT_ROWS); the 5440 B bfp8 row fits one packet

missing: the MoE block's L1 arena is allocated between moe_head and routed_experts_combine: any op launched there must put its CBs in the arena (static CBs clash)
RISC loads of L1 data written by the packer miss the cache line by line after invalidate_l1_cache (~200 cycles for 16 words): move small pieces with local NoC writes

overseer.evidence: no padding or duplicated work: the bfp8 row carries exactly the packer's bytes (5440 B), the pack reads each bf16 row piece once (8-tile column parts, not 4 cores re-reading a unit)
pack_bfp8_rows (the only Python-built op added) runs through ttnn.bringup.prepare_program / run_prepared (fp8_rows_ttnn/bfp8_rows.py _prepared); the flat expert / combine are C++ ops
no fork regression suites run; only the new model-level tests (tests/test_dispatch_fp8.py, tests/perf/test_dispatch_width.py) and the measure parts
